smell: That timeline matters because Beaman never got the ordinary stretch of Saturdays that turns a young defensive lineman into a dependable part of a rotation.
The available reporting does not identify a confirmed replacement or provide a new depth chart.
Alabama now has to judge its defensive line without the player who was supposed to supply evidence about his own development.
The next useful information will come from personnel decisions, not broad assurances.
By Alabama’s September 2026 opener, the depth chart and the first rotation should show whether the unit found a dependable way to divide that work.

rows.label: V3 · castellanos-texas-tech (analysis-worthy; depth brief)
smell: Tommy Castellanos has committed to Texas Tech, according to On3's Pete Nakos, giving the Red Raiders a 38-game quarterback behind Will Hammond, who is recovering from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 season.

rows.label: V1 Wire story · castellanos-texas-tech
smell: The move created immediate questions about whether he would replace Will Hammond as the Red Raiders’ starting quarterback.
Texas Tech has not announced a different quarterback plan.
The former Florida State quarterback is headed to Lubbock, but his arrival does not currently change Texas Tech’s starting plan.
Will Hammond remains the quarterback to watch.

rows.label: V1 house piece (review pack) · castellanos-texas-tech
smell: That uncertainty isn't a flaw in the story. It is the story.
The point is narrower. Castellanos's value cannot be measured only by whether he can execute the current offense. Texas Tech has to measure what the current offense can become with him in it.
The useful answer lives in the football, not the announcement.
Texas Tech should adapt enough to use Castellanos's running threat, but not so much that it abandons the quarterback who currently leads the room.
The Red Raiders need one offense with enough flexibility for both possibilities, not two separate systems competing for Saturday snaps.
